An English crib of the Latin text, semi-literal, made for this database in 2026 with Claude, a large language model (LLM) made by Anthropic. It keeps close to the wording of the original and uses the established English of Anglo-Latin legal, liturgical and canon-law formulae. It is an aid to reading the original, not a published translation. Square brackets mark Liebermann’s additions to the text or, now and then, words supplied for the sense; “[?]” marks a doubtful reading

div.head: ECf 8.2a
div.ab: Et qui eam detinuerit, per iusticiam sancte ecclesie et regis, si necesse fuerit, ad redditionem cogatur.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 632 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.

note.seg: þæs cynges gerefa ⁊ þæs bisceopes; II Eg. 3 (daraus VIII Atr. 8; I Cn. 8; Hn. 11, 2). Den Erstlingszehnt erzwingt durch Anathema die Englische Synode von 1138
þæs cynges gerefa ⁊ þæs bisceopes; II Eg. 3 (whence VIII Atr. 8; I Cn. 8; Hn. 11, 2). The English synod of 1138 enforces the tithe of first-fruits by anathema

div.ab: And he who withholds it, let him be compelled to render it by the justice of holy Church and of the king, if necessary.
